ut_trash_compactor_the.blurb: A small sport crag tucked into a narrow corridor above Maple Canyon Road in central Utah, with about a dozen routes. The grade range is wide, from a 5.3 warm-up pitch up to 5.10, but most of the lines sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers comfortable around that level more than first-timers. The corridor holds shade, which makes it a pleasant place to be on hot summer days. The routes start near a dark water streak where the walls pinch together, and the walk in is short.

ut_monochromatic.blurb: A small bouldering zone in the Meadows at Bunker Creek, near Brian Head in southwest Utah. About a dozen problems are spread over three good boulders, in a shady spot at the bottom of a little valley east of the main cluster. Grades run from V0 up to V11, with a bunch of problems around V5 to V6 and only a few easy ones, so it leans toward stronger boulderers. Expect cool conditions at this high elevation, which suits late spring and early fall visits.

ut_mill_canyon_west.blurb: A compact sport wall in Mill Canyon, a quiet side canyon off Echo Canyon in Utah's Wasatch Back. It holds around a dozen bolted lines, and nearly all of them are hard: roughly nine sit in the 5.12 range, with only a couple of 5.11s and a single 5.10 to warm up on. That makes it a destination for experienced sport climbers rather than beginners. Because the canyon sees little traffic, expect routes that could use more cleaning and few other parties.

ut_clint_eastwood_wall.blurb: A small sport wall at the mouth of Bear Hollow, a side canyon of Echo Canyon in Utah's Wasatch Back. Roughly a dozen routes run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with most in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it works for newer leaders as well as people stepping up. The rock is conglomerate and slabby, with cobbles and pockets for holds, and a helmet is a good idea. The wall faces southwest and catches sun most of the day. It is only a short stroll from the roadside pullout.

ut_cragmont.blurb: A trad area on sandstone near the Mount Carmel Tunnel on the east side of Zion National Park. Twelve routes are known, nearly all in the 5.10 range, with one 5.11 and two 5.12s, so it suits climbers who are already solid on crack and face gear leads. Zion sandstone is soft and easily damaged when wet, so wait out rain and for the rock to dry before you climb. Bring webbing to back up rappel anchors, as is normal across the park.

ut_graveside_matter_slab.blurb: A slab in Cedar Canyon outside Cedar City, part of the Graveside Matter Wall complex on sandstone. Most of the dozen routes are bolted, with just a couple of trad lines. The climbing is technical and mostly low-angle friction, with the odd steeper, more featured line. Grades start easy at 5.6 and 5.8 but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.11, and a handful reach into the 5.12s and 5.13s, so it rewards confident footwork. Expect a trail walk up the canyon past a boulder and a creek crossing to reach the base.

ut_cherry_creek_boulders.blurb: A lightly developed bouldering spot in Cherry Creek Canyon, a quiet, scenic canyon in Utah's Cache Valley. About a dozen problems are scattered around, running from V2 up to V9, with the middle of the range around V4 and V5 and relatively little at the easy end. The boulders sit at roughly 6,200 feet, which makes it a popular summer spot, though photos show people bouldering here in late fall and winter too. Expect a modest walk up a trail from the end of the road.
